resources.string: Connection lost — reconnecting in %1$d s (attempt %2$d of %3$d)…
%1$s Reconnecting failed %2$d times. Tap Reconnect to try again.
The connection keeps dropping. Check that the adapter sits firmly in the OBD port and is powered, then reconnect.
Not connected to an OBD adapter.
Bluetooth was turned off, so the OBD connection was closed.
Bluetooth is off. Switch it on and try again.
Bluetooth permission missing: allow “Nearby devices” for this app and try again.
The adapter address “%1$s” is not valid.

Couldn’t connect to “%1$s”. Check that the adapter is plugged in and powered (LED on), that it is in range, and that no other phone or app is connected to it (it accepts only one connection). Unplugging it for a few seconds often helps.
“%1$s” offers no known OBD data service over Bluetooth LE. It may not be an OBD adapter, or it may need a Bluetooth (Classic) connection instead.
Can’t reach the Wi-Fi adapter at %1$s. Join the adapter’s Wi-Fi network (often “WiFi_OBDII” or “V-LINK”) in the phone’s Wi-Fi settings and stay connected even though it has no internet.
Shown while the app is connected to an OBD adapter or recording OBD data
